destination.name: Paris
destination.tipping: Service is included by law in menu prices. Tipping is optional; rounding up or leaving a few euros for good service is a courtesy.
destination.tap_water: Safe. Restaurants should give a free carafe of tap water (une carafe d'eau) on request.

entry.summary: France is in the Schengen area. The EU Entry/Exit System has been fully operational at all Schengen external borders since 10 April 2026. ETIAS is expected to start in Q4 2026 with the exact date still to be announced. Check official EU pages before you travel.

safety_snapshot.note: Pickpocketing, especially on the Metro and at major sights, and tourist-targeted street scams are the main risks. Violent crime against tourists is uncommon.

transport.name: RER B airport ticket (CDG to central Paris)
transport.note: The Paris Region-Airports ticket (14 EUR) has covered CDG rail travel since 1 Jan 2026. Load it on a Navigo Easy card or app. Stops include Gare du Nord (about 30 min) and Chatelet-Les Halles (about 35 min).

transport.name: Official taxi, CDG to Paris (flat fare)
transport.note: Flat fare by decree: 56 EUR to the Right Bank, 65 EUR to the Left Bank, same day or night, up to four passengers with luggage. Disneyland and other destinations outside Paris use the meter.

transport.name: Metro / RER / train single ticket (inside Paris)
transport.note: Sources differ between 2.50 and 2.55 EUR; confirm on the Ile-de-France Mobilites site. Bus and tram single about 2.05 EUR. Navigo Day pass about 12.30 EUR; weekly Navigo about 32.40 EUR (all zones).

transport.name: RoissyBus (discontinued)
transport.note: One 2026 source reports the classic RoissyBus to Opera ended on 1 March 2026. Do not list it until confirmed. Bus 9517 is described as a replacement.

safety_zones.name: Eiffel Tower and Trocadero
safety_zones.note: Petition clipboards, gold ring, unofficial ticket sellers, pickpockets in queues.

safety_zones.name: Louvre pyramid and queues
safety_zones.note: Pickpockets in queues and crowded rooms; petition teams.

safety_zones.name: Chatelet and Metro line 1 corridor
safety_zones.note: Crowded trains, phone snatching as doors close.

safety_zones.name: Gare du Nord area
safety_zones.note: Taxi touts, pickpockets, ticket-machine helpers. Use official taxi ranks.

safety_zones.name: Pigalle and Barbes at night
safety_zones.note: Nightlife area with aggressive touts and pickpockets; take care late at night.

places.name: Eiffel Tower
places.why: Paris's signature landmark with views from the second floor and summit.
places.price: Adult (25+) about 14.80 EUR stairs to 2nd floor, about 23.50 EUR lift to 2nd floor, about 36.70 EUR summit by lift. Youth and child prices are lower.
tips: Official site: toureiffel.paris. From 29 Sept 2026 stairs tickets also need an advance reservation.
The summit and the stairs are not suitable for limited mobility.
places.access: Lift to 2nd floor and summit; stairs not accessible.

places.name: Louvre Museum
places.why: The world's most visited museum: Mona Lisa, Venus de Milo, Egyptian and Islamic collections.
places.price: 22 EUR for EU/EEA visitors; 32 EUR for most visitors from outside the EEA since 13 Jan 2026.
places.best: First slot or evening opening day
tips: Reserve a time slot online.
Pick two wings, not the whole museum.

places.name: Notre-Dame de Paris
places.why: Gothic cathedral reopened after restoration; free to enter.
places.price: Entry free. The tower climb is ticketed with advance reservation.
tips: Towers need an advance reservation per a 2026 pass guide.

places.name: Sainte-Chapelle
places.price: Higher price for non-EU visitors since Jan 2026 (about 6 EUR more); base price: verify.
tips: Security line is separate from the timed ticket; arrive early.
places.access: Upper chapel by stairs; lower chapel step-free.

places.name: Arc de Triomphe
places.why: Napoleonic monument with a rooftop view down the Champs-Elysees.
tips: Use the pedestrian underpass to reach it. Never cross the roundabout traffic.

places.name: Musee d'Orsay
places.why: Impressionist masterpieces inside a former railway station.
tips: Reserve a time slot.

places.name: Sacre-Coeur and Montmartre
places.why: White basilica on the hill, artists' squares and village lanes.
tips: Approach by the side streets; keep hands in pockets on the base steps.
places.access: Many steps; a funicular uses a standard transit ticket.

places.name: Le Marais
places.why: Historic lanes, boutiques, falafel and the Place des Vosges.
tips: Many shops open on Sundays when others are closed.

places.name: Luxembourg Gardens
places.why: Green chairs, a pond with model boats, a perfect pause.
tips: Take a book and a green chair.

places.name: Musee de l'Orangerie
places.why: Monet's Water Lilies in oval rooms.
tips: A shorter, calmer art stop than the Louvre.

places.name: Palais Garnier (Opera)
places.why: Gilded 19th-century opera house with a grand staircase.
places.price: Higher price for non-EU visitors since Jan 2026 (verify).
tips: Check closures on show days.

places.name: Pere Lachaise Cemetery
places.why: Famous graves among tree-lined lanes; a peaceful walk.
tips: A place of remembrance. Keep voices low and respect mourners.

places.name: Canal Saint-Martin
places.why: Footbridges, cafes and picnics along the water; very Parisian.
tips: Locals picnic here. Take your litter.

places.name: Latin Quarter and Shakespeare and Company
places.why: Bookshops, student streets, the famous English-language bookstore.
tips: Avoid restaurants with touts on the narrow tourist streets.

places.name: Marche d'Aligre
places.why: A local food market with cheeses, fruit and a covered hall.
tips: Check market days and hours; the outdoor market runs most mornings.

places.name: Catacombs of Paris
tips: Buy official timed tickets in advance. Not suitable for claustrophobia or limited mobility.
places.access: Not accessible: spiral staircase and uneven floors.

places.name: Palace of Versailles (day trip)
places.why: The royal palace, Hall of Mirrors and gardens.
places.price: Up to about 35 EUR peak for non-EU visitors since Jan 2026 (verify).
tips: Take RER C. Use a timed ticket.

places.name: Centre Pompidou (renovation closure)
places.why: Modern art museum in its distinctive inside-out building.
tips: Reported as closed for a long renovation that began in 2025 and runs until about 2030. Verify before listing it in any itinerary.

food.name: Baguette, croissant and the boulangerie
food.desc: Look for a baguette 'tradition' and a croissant au beurre. Boulangeries often have a sandwich and drink 'formule' at lunch.
food.tip: Greet with 'Bonjour' when you enter. It matters.

food.name: Bistro classics
food.desc: Steak frites, onion soup, duck confit, croque monsieur, plat du jour.
food.tip: The plat du jour or a lunch 'formule' is the best value. Ask for 'une carafe d'eau' for free tap water.

food.name: Crepes and galettes
food.desc: Savoury buckwheat galettes and sweet crepes, a Breton tradition around Montparnasse and the Marais.

food.name: Bouillon Chartier
food.desc: Historic big-hall bouillon serving classic French dishes at modest prices.

food.name: Breizh Cafe (Marais)
food.desc: Well-known creperie with galettes and cider.

food.name: L'As du Fallafel
food.desc: Famous falafel takeaway in the old Jewish quarter.

food.name: Du Pain et des Idees
food.desc: Beloved artisan bakery near Canal Saint-Martin.

food.name: Berthillon
food.desc: Classic ice cream on Ile Saint-Louis.

food.name: Stohrer
food.desc: One of the oldest patisseries in Paris.

food.name: Bonjour, the carafe and the terrace price
food.desc: Say bonjour on entering shops and cafes. Tap water is free on request. Prices are lower standing at the bar (comptoir) than seated on a terrace.
food.tip: Service is included. Tipping is optional.

hidden_spots.name: Passage des Panoramas and Galerie Vivienne
hidden_spots.why: Covered 19th-century arcades with tea rooms and old shops, a quiet escape from the big boulevards.
hidden_spots.etiquette: Shops and tea rooms; keep the passages calm.

hidden_spots.name: Parc des Buttes-Chaumont
hidden_spots.why: Hilly park with a lake, a cliff and a hilltop temple; strongly local.

hidden_spots.name: Rue Cremieux
hidden_spots.why: A pedestrian street of pastel houses that is popular for photos.
hidden_spots.etiquette: Residents have asked for quiet. No loud groups, drones or photo shoots.

hidden_spots.name: Square du Vert-Galant
hidden_spots.why: A small park at the western tip of the Ile de la Cite with a river-level view.

hidden_spots.name: Promenade Plantee (Coulee verte Rene-Dumont)
hidden_spots.why: An elevated garden walk on an old railway viaduct, a calm alternative to street-level crowds.
hidden_spots.etiquette: Shared walkway; keep to one side.

scams.title: The 'found' gold ring
scams.how: Someone pretends to pick a gold ring off the ground, offers it to you, then asks for money or a reward. The ring is worthless.
scams.avoid: Do not take it. Say no and walk away.
scams.if_happened: Do not argue; walk away to a busy place. Report persistent harassment to police.

scams.title: Friendship-bracelet 'string men' at Sacre-Coeur
scams.how: At the base of the Sacre-Coeur steps, someone grabs your wrist and ties a string bracelet, then demands payment.
scams.avoid: Keep your hands in your pockets or bag, say a firm no and keep walking up. Use the side routes.
scams.if_happened: You are not obliged to pay for something forced on you. Walk away to a busy spot and report it.

scams.title: Clipboard petition and distraction teams
scams.how: Groups ask you to sign a petition or donate. While you read, accomplices go through your bag or ask for money.
scams.avoid: Do not stop. A clear 'no thank you' and keep walking. Keep your bag closed and in front.
scams.if_happened: Check your belongings immediately and report theft to police.

scams.title: Shell game (cup and ball) near tourist sites
scams.how: A street 'game' appears winnable but is rigged. Pickpockets work the crowd of onlookers.
scams.avoid: Do not play and do not stop to watch.
scams.if_happened: If you lost money, you cannot get it back; check your pockets and walk away.

scams.title: Airport taxi overcharging and unofficial drivers
scams.how: Unofficial drivers approach you inside the terminal or station and quote high prices.
scams.avoid: Use the official taxi rank. Flat fares between CDG and Paris are 56 EUR (Right Bank) and 65 EUR (Left Bank), day or night, for up to four passengers. Or take RER B for 14 EUR.
scams.if_happened: Note plate and time and report to police or the taxi authority; dispute the card payment if needed.

scams.title: Metro ticket-machine helpers and turnstile pickpockets
scams.how: Helpers offer to operate the machine and then want payment or swap your ticket. Pickpockets use crowded doors and turnstiles.
scams.avoid: Decline help and use the app or a card. Keep phones in front pockets near doors.
scams.if_happened: Block cards, report to the station staff or police and use Find My Device.

scams.title: Pickpockets on busy lines and at major sights
scams.how: Thieves operate on Metro lines such as 1 and 4, in the Louvre queue and at the Eiffel Tower and Montmartre.
scams.avoid: Zip bags and keep them in front. Keep phones away from doors and edges.
scams.if_happened: Block cards, report to police for an insurance report.

scams.title: Fake or unofficial tickets and resellers
scams.how: Sellers and websites offer 'skip-the-line' tickets at inflated prices or invalid tickets.
scams.avoid: Buy only from the official site of each attraction. Check the web address carefully.
scams.if_happened: Keep screenshots and ask your card issuer for a chargeback.

scams.title: Overpriced terraces and tourist menus
scams.how: Terraces facing major monuments can charge several times the usual price for a coffee or meal.
scams.avoid: Check prices on the board before sitting. Walk two streets away from major sights.
scams.if_happened: Ask for an itemised bill; you can dispute clear overcharging.

scams.title: Fake QR codes and fake accommodation listings
scams.how: Stickers covering real QR codes lead to payment pages that steal card data. Fake apartment listings take deposits for flats that do not exist.
scams.avoid: Check for stickers on printed codes. Book accommodation only through trusted platforms and never pay by direct transfer.
scams.if_happened: Contact your card issuer and report to police.

rules.title: Entry and EU border systems
rules.summary: France is in Schengen. The EU Entry/Exit System has been fully operational since 10 April 2026. ETIAS is expected in Q4 2026; the exact start date is still to be announced.
rules.instead: Check your nationality's requirements on the official EU site.

rules.title: Higher prices for visitors from outside the EU
rules.summary: Since 13 January 2026 several French institutions (including the Louvre, Versailles, Chambord, Sainte-Chapelle and the Opera Garnier) charge higher prices to visitors from outside the EU/EEA. The Louvre is 32 EUR versus 22 EUR.
rules.instead: Check the official site for your category and carry proof if asked.

rules.title: Timed reservations are required at many sites
rules.summary: The Louvre, Musee d'Orsay, Versailles, Sainte-Chapelle and the Orangerie require an advance time slot, even with a museum pass.
rules.instead: Reserve online from each official site.

rules.title: Eiffel Tower stairs now need a reservation
rules.summary: The official Eiffel Tower site says advance reservations are required for stairs tickets from 29 September 2026. Summit and lift tickets are sold online and on site.
rules.instead: Book on the official site, toureiffel.paris.

rules.title: Service is included
rules.summary: Menu prices include service by law. Extra tipping is optional.
rules.instead: Round up or leave a few euros for good service.

rules.title: Free tap water on request
rules.summary: Restaurants should give you a carafe of tap water (une carafe d'eau) at no charge with a meal if you ask.
rules.instead: Ask for 'une carafe d'eau' instead of paying for bottled water.

rules.title: Mandatory airport taxi flat fares
rules.summary: Between CDG and Paris the official flat fare is 56 EUR to the Right Bank and 65 EUR to the Left Bank, mandatory, day or night, for up to four passengers (fixed by decree for 2026).
rules.instead: Refuse any higher quote and use the official rank.

rules.title: Keep a valid ticket until you exit
rules.summary: Inspectors check tickets on trains and RER. Travelling without a valid ticket leads to a fine.
rules.instead: Validate or tap in and keep the ticket or card until the end of the trip.

rules.title: Drones are heavily restricted in Paris
rules.summary: Paris and its surroundings are highly restricted airspace for drones. Flying without authorisation can lead to fines or seizure.
rules.instead: Do not fly in or near central Paris.

rules.title: Smoking restrictions outdoors
rules.summary: France has been extending smoking bans to more outdoor public places (such as near schools and some parks and beaches). Check signs on the spot.

rules.title: Alcohol and public drinking
rules.summary: The legal purchase age is 18. Drinking outdoors is tolerated in many places, but some zones, quays and events have temporary bans.
rules.instead: Check local signs. Do not drink and disturb neighbours at night.

rules.title: Guiding in museums and monuments is regulated
rules.summary: Giving paid guided tours inside museums and historic monuments in France is reserved to guides who hold the national professional card (guide-conferencier). Informal paid tours elsewhere may also be regulated.
rules.instead: Use licensed guides for site tours. Label informal companions as such. Needs legal verification before launch.

rules.title: Respect image rights
rules.summary: France has strong image-right rules. Do not publish identifiable photos of strangers, especially children, without consent.
rules.instead: Keep people out of the frame or ask first.

rules.title: Modest dress in churches
rules.summary: Churches ask for respectful clothing and quiet.

rules.title: Security screening and bag limits
rules.summary: Major sites screen bags and may refuse large luggage.
rules.instead: Travel light and check each site's rules.

rules.title: Respect at cemeteries
rules.summary: Pere Lachaise is an active cemetery and a place of remembrance.
rules.instead: Keep noise down and do not touch or climb on graves.
